decision: Run the four frozen-world-parameter controls after the native frozen-arm preflight passes.
evidence: All four passive days exactly reproduce v4 costs, budgets and initializers.
Post-shock historical current context increases error versus saved, but genuine next-packet Bellman errors are nearly identical.
Eight full optimizer updates propagate local calibration into critics and actors, while the incremental executed holding change remains very small.
Next-packet shadow TD differences do not establish realized passenger benefits; freezing neural world parameters directly isolates refitting in a real control rollout.
comparator: v4 action_model, same original two seeds crossed with stable and local_speed_drop
intervention: Freeze initial neural source/direct/residual world parameters; keep family selection, trust QDelta, replay and policy learning active; local readout disabled.
next_decision: Compare full-day and18300–24000 passenger costs separately in both scenarios, plus prequential errors and trust. Consistently worse refitting motivates revising the neural update; better refitting keeps it and focuses revision on local-to-global action consequences. Mixed results retain both hypotheses and do not justify a formal expansion.
scope: Two original development seeds; no claim of independent confirmation or isolation of fresh-data benefit from continued policy optimization.
